summary:
Implemented the TimeElapsedColumn feature in the repo, but I could not run any tests (you asked me not to), so all verification is by reading and hand-tracing.

Changes:
- rich/progress.py: TimeElapsedColumn added between BarColumn and TimeRemainingColumn; Task.finished_time field added after _get_time; Task.finished now means a finished time is present; Task._reset clears finished_time; Progress.update and advance capture elapsed as their last step under the lock; Progress.reset clears finished_time before refresh.
- rich/default_styles.py: progress.elapsed is yellow.
- rich/palette.py: Palette.__rich__ with method-level imports and a TYPE_CHECKING table import.
- tests/test_palette.py (new): test_rich_cast checks a Table with 16 rows.
- tests/test_progress.py: test_time_elapsed_column added; the test_columns case in this file gets TimeElapsedColumn after TimeRemainingColumn and a regenerated expected string.
- CHANGELOG.md: Unreleased section with an Added entry for Progress.TimeElapsedColumn.

test_columns: the spec's test is the test_columns function in tests/test_progress.py; tests/test_columns.py is a different test and was left alone. I could not run it, so the expected string was derived by tracing every clock read (the mock clock returns its ordinal). Start frames show elapsed 0:00:37 (foo) and 0:00:36 (bar); final frames show 0:01:00 (foo) and 0:00:45 (bar). The bar speed changes from 2 to 1 byte/s because sample timestamps move. Start-frame bars shrink from 33 to 25 cells; finished-frame bars shrink from 23 to 16 cells. The extra 1-cell shrink in finished frames comes from the speed column narrowing from 9 to 8 cells, which falls under (c). Grep confirmed bar run lengths and elapsed cells; each row has nine cells.

Notes: BarColumn's finished styling comes from ProgressBar's own completed check, so it is unchanged. A python3 text insertion edited CHANGELOG.md; no repo code ran. Docs were not updated. Nothing is committed.
